elaine: Heads-up — after the kernel-selector swap on canary yesterday we saw a ~12% drop in decode throughput and 3 transient OOMs on p3x nodes. KV-prefill allocations ballooned in a few traces.

raj: ugh. do we have profiler output or traces? which kernel was swapped?

elaine: swapped to fastmat-v2 (microkernel set B) to improve matmul latency. looks like an unintended side-effect on prefill: extra temp buffers for fp16->qint8 path. attaching a clipped perf snippet below.

elaine: ```
Perf summary (canary vs baseline):
- avg token throughput: baseline 1800 t/s -> canary 1580 t/s (-12.2%)
- 95th p99 latency: baseline 38ms -> canary 44ms
- mean GPU mem transient alloc per request: baseline 42 MB -> canary 88 MB
Hot stacks (canary):
- fastmat_v2::im2col_temp_alloc
- kv_prefill::materialize_prefix
- decoder::kv_insert_batch
OOM logs (snippet):
[2024-06-08T20:12:34Z] gpu0 ERROR: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory (requested 34.0 MiB)
Stack: decoder::decode_step -> fastmat_v2::dispatch -> kv_prefill::materialize_prefix
```

maria: that jump in transient alloc looks like fragmentation + larger scratch per kernel. prefill path materializes entire prefix chunk before streaming -> a lot of simultaneous small slabs.

ben: can we confirm whether the new kernel's scratch size scales with sequence length or batch size? if it's per-request and not per-batch, it explodes.

elaine: quick check: fastmat-v2's scratch = O(seq_len * D_block) and currently we don't share that scratch across requests when prefill runs in parallel. for large prefixes (>=512) it multiplies.

raj: two practical mitigations:
1) per-request KV prefill cap (e.g., cap materialized kv per request to 8MB) — trim older prefix segments to avoid huge one-offs.
2) defer full materialize -> stream decode with small staging buffer (prefill-on-demand hybrid).

maria: +1 for per-request cap. also suggest coalescing small slabs in allocator (slab-coalesce pass) so fragmentation cost is bounded. we saw ~30% wasted space in simulator when we had many 3-12KB slabs.

ben: i can prototype allocator tweak: add a thin "reuse-pool" for kernel scratch that is keyed by kernel-type+shape. if a new kernel asks for scratch within 10% of an existing slab, reuse instead of cudaMalloc. reduces churn.

elaine: that would help. another low-friction step: limit concurrent prefill workers to N (default 16) down to 6 on the canary fleets — cuts peak transient mem.

ops-bot: Deployment note: Canaries on p3x-8 currently running image redwood/runtime:canary-fastmatv2-20240608. Rollback window scheduled in 30m if errors >= 2.

raj: also flag: eviction behavior currently prioritizes oldest-per-prefix, not size. so when we cap per-request kv, evictor might still keep many small hot entries and blow memory. need size-aware eviction with frag score.

maria: propose eviction heuristic: score = lambda_age * age + lambda_size * size_in_bytes + lambda_frag * frag_factor. tune lambdas to prefer removing high-frag blocks first. frag_factor measured as internal slab waste percentage.

ben: i ran a quick sim overnight with 10k synthetic requests (mixed prefix sizes). results: per-request cap 8MB + slab-coalesce + reuse-pool => peak mem -38%, OOMs -> 0, median latency +1.8% (acceptable). without reuse-pool peak mem -14%.

elaine: can we land a short-term plan tonight?
- Immediately: reduce canary prefill concurrency to 6, set per-request prefill cap=8MB, enable kernel scratch reuse flag (off by default) in canary.
- Medium: allocator slab-coalesce + eviction frag_score rollout to staging.
- Long: refactor prefill to hybrid streaming and add compile-time kernel scratch upper bounds.

raj: SGTM. small ask — include a debug metric: per-request transient_alloc_bytes so we can graph tail behavior per model.

maria: i'll add the metric and a Grafana panel for it (by EOD).

ben: i'll open a PR for reuse-pool + config flag. linking perf sim in PR.

elaine: i'll push the canary knobs now (rolling 6 at a time) and bump alert thresholds. will report back in 20m.

ops-bot: [2024-06-08T20:25:10Z] deploy: rolling update started (6/48 hosts) image=redwood/runtime:canary-fastmatv2-20240608 knobs={prefill_concurrency:6, prefill_cap_bytes:8388608, scratch_reuse:enabled}

elaine: quick status: first 6 rolled, no OOMs yet, throughput still slightly down but stable. continuing rollout paused at 12 hosts to gather traces.

raj: thanks team. let's follow-up tomorrow with a short postmortem and perf run on a staging fleet with the sim workload.

maria: noted — i'll ensure eviction metrics, frag_score breakdown, and per-request transient_alloc_bytes are in the dashboard.

ben: PR #5123 opened: runtime: scratch reuse pool + slab-coalesce prototype + benchmark. includes config toggles and unit tests.

elaine: perfect. will link logs/traces in the incident ticket. :thumbsup:
